problems.title: Two intersections determine three coefficients
problems.question: The line y=kx and parabola y=−x²+bx+c meet at (0,0) and (−4,−12). Find k,b,c.
problems.idea: Insert each point into both equations.
formulas: k=y/x for a nonzero x; the parabola at x=0 has y=c.
steps: The origin gives c=0. The other point gives k=(−12)/(−4)=3.

problems.title: A finite geometric-sum identity
problems.question: Solve $(1+x+x^2)(1+x+\cdots+x^{10})=(1+x+\cdots+x^6)^2$.
problems.idea: Use the finite-sum formula away from x=1, then check that excluded value separately.
steps: Subtracting the right side yields −x³(x⁴−1)²=0. The real candidates are 0,1,−1.
x=1 fails the original equation because 3·11≠7².
Direct substitution confirms x=0 and x=−1.

problems.title: A weighted sum of median vectors
problems.question: A₁,B₁,C₁ are the side midpoints of triangle ABC. Vector 3AA₁+4BB₁+5CC₁=(2,1). Find AC.
problems.idea: Expand each midpoint vector using position vectors.
formulas: AA₁=(B+C−2A)/2, and similarly for the other medians.
steps: After collecting coefficients the sum is (3/2)A+0B−(3/2)C=(3/2)(A−C).
Thus the length of AC is 2/3 times the length of (2,1).

problems.title: A quadrilateral with both an incircle and circumcircle
problems.question: ABCD has both an incircle and a circumcircle. AB=2,BC=4,CD=5. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use opposite side sums for tangency and the cyclic area formula.

problems.title: Move a parabola’s vertex as close to the origin as possible
problems.question: For which a is the vertex of y=x²−2ax+a²+a+1 closest to the origin?
problems.idea: Complete the square to locate the vertex.

problems.title: Workers join one at a time
problems.question: Six workers can finish a job in 10 hours. They start at 11:00; at 17:00 one worker joins, then one more each hour. When is the job completed?
problems.idea: Measure the whole job in worker-hours.
steps: By 17:00, six hours have passed and 6·6=36 worker-hours are done.
From 17:00 to 18:00, seven workers add 7; from 18:00 to 19:00, eight add 8. Total done is 51.
Nine workers from 19:00 to 20:00 complete the remaining 9 worker-hours.

problems.title: Two division statements about a progression
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression, the ninth term divided by the second is 5. The thirteenth divided by the sixth has quotient 2 and remainder 5. Find the first term and difference.
problems.idea: Translate the statements into two linear equations.
steps: Solving yields d=4 and a=3. The second and sixth terms are 7 and 23, so the divisions are valid.

problems.title: A square sharing a side with a regular hexagon
problems.question: A square and regular hexagon share a side, with two square vertices inside the hexagon. Their centres are distance 2 apart. Find the hexagon’s area.
problems.idea: Both centres lie on the perpendicular bisector of the shared side.
formulas: Hexagon apothem=s√3/2; square-centre distance from side=s/2; hexagon area=3√3s²/2.
steps: The centres are on the same side of the common edge, so their distance is s(√3−1)/2=2.

problems.title: A circle on an isosceles triangle’s leg
problems.question: AB=BC=8, AC=4. The circle with diameter BC meets AB again at M and AC again at N. Find area AMN.
problems.idea: Angles in a semicircle make CM and BN altitudes.
formulas: AN=AC/2=2; cos A=AC/(2AB)=1/4; AM=AC cos A.
steps: BN is the altitude of the isosceles triangle, so N is the midpoint of AC.

problems.title: Maximize the area of a parameter rectangle
problems.question: For $-5<a<2$, maximize the area defined by $5+a-|2y|\ge0$ and $|x|\le|a-2|/2$.
problems.idea: Read the rectangle’s full width and height from the inequalities.
steps: The maximum is attained at a=−3/2, which lies inside the required interval.
